finding.claim: GET /mirror fetches an attacker-supplied URL whose host is checked only by a suffix match (endswith("example.com")) with no dot boundary and no resolved-IP check, enabling blind SSRF to internal hosts or metadata endpoints.
finding.source: Query parameter `url` on the unauthenticated GET /mirror route (mirror.py:11).

trace.note: url: str taken from the query string on an unauthenticated route.
host = urlparse(url).hostname or "" parses the URL.
Check is host.endswith("example.com"); matches evilexample.com or xexample.com, so an attacker-registered domain passes.
Fetches the original unparsed url string, not the validated host; no resolved-IP, private-range, or metadata-address filtering.

finding.guards_checked: Host suffix check (mirror.py:13) lacks a dot boundary; ALLOWED_SUFFIX=".example.com" (mirror.py:7) is defined but unused. Userinfo (https://example.com@evil.com) and fragment (#.example.com) tricks are rejected by urlparse. httpx AsyncClient defaults to follow_redirects=False, so redirects are not an open path. httpx only supports http/https, so file:// and similar schemes are not reachable. No DNS-rebinding protection (IP is not pinned). Response returns only len(r.text), so the SSRF is blind with a length oracle. Unverified: possible urlparse vs httpx parser differential (e.g. backslash in authority) not tested.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, which has no dot boundary, so it passes evilexample.com. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) is defined but never used. The fetch at mirror.py:16 uses the raw `url` string with no IP or private-range filtering, and the route at mirror.py:10-11 has no authentication.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) reaches `c.get(url)` (mirror.py:16) on an unauthenticated route, and the only host check, `endswith("example.com")` (mirror.py:13), has no dot boundary, so an attacker-registered domain like evilexample.com passes; that domain's DNS can resolve to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, making the blind SSRF reachable as claimed. The candidate's trace matches the code line for line.
